title: Wild Bill Donovan and the original crash-retrieval protocols
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Wild Bill Donovan and the original crash-retrieval protocols, about 1930s-1940s at United States (no place named), and reports it citing named sources. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Chief OSS member and another CIA founder, Wild Bill Donovan, who journalist Chris Sharp notes was likely not only involved in the Magenta crash retrieval, but in setting up original protocols for UFO crash retrievals, was also a Knight of Malta.

plain: William "Wild Bill" Donovan led the OSS, America's spy agency in World War Two, and helped found the CIA that came after it. The podcast host Jesse Michels, drawing on a journalist named Chris Sharp, says Donovan was probably involved in recovering a crashed craft in Magenta, Italy, in the 1930s or 40s, and in writing the first US rules for retrieving crashed UFOs. Michels adds that Donovan was also a Knight of Malta, a member of an old Catholic order, which matters if one thinks such groups shaped the secrecy.
